issues.body: `sparq_gpu_is_still_unpublished` still checks only whether a comment-stripped line starts with `publish` and contains `false`. A valid unused key such as `publish-note = false` satisfies that predicate even if `publish = false` is removed or changed to `publish = true`. Cargo would then treat the package as publishable while this security-deferral trigger remains green, contradicting the enforcement claims in `lib.rs` and `research/threat-model.md`.
issues.fix_hint: Use the already-produced Cargo metadata and select the `sparq-gpu` package by workspace package identity, then require its `publish` field to be an empty array (Cargo metadata's representation of `publish = false`). Add a focused regression test or fixture proving that an absent/true `publish` setting plus an unrelated `publish-... = false` key is rejected.
issues.title: Publication tripwire still accepts unrelated manifest keys

verdict.summary: Round 3's major finding remains materially unchanged. The dependency tripwire is metadata-backed, but the publication tripwire still scans manifest text and accepts unrelated keys such as `publish-note = false`; therefore Cargo may consider `sparq-gpu` publishable while the test passes. Because the same major issue remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
